author: ValWood
body:
There is a difference in activity between yeast  Slm3 and metazoan ortholog human TRMU
as they target a different but analogous modified uridine

Human is GO:0061708 tRNA-5-taurinomethyluridine 2-sulfurtransferase   ( τm⁵U)
Yeast is  GO:0103016 tRNA-uridine 2-sulfurtransferase activity (cmnm⁵s²U34  (not τm⁵U)


Currently this isn't PAINTED, but the yeast/pombe orthologs are annotated in PomBase SGD and UniProt with the human activity
I'm opening a ticket here so that once fixed @marcfeuermann  can PAINT to the correct terms to the 2 clades.

@edwong57  could you revise the SGD annotation? Here are some papers which should provide the correct term


[Mitochondria-specific RNA-modifying enzymes responsible for the biosynthesis of the wobble base in mitochondrial tRNAs. Implications for the molecular pathogenesis of human mitochondrial diseases.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15509579/)
Umeda N, Suzuki T, Yukawa M, Ohya Y, Shindo H, Watanabe K, Suzuki T.
J Biol Chem. 2005 Jan 14;280(2):1613-24. doi: 10.1074/jbc.M409306200. Epub 2004 Oct 26.
PMID: 15509579

should confirm  that the yeast modification is cmnm⁵s²U34 

@Antonialock  for UniProt:  note there aren't GO but there is function note transfer by similarity.

I am removing the PomBase  ISO to yeast  GO:0061708 and changing the correct NAS to GO:0103016  to  an ISO to yeast SAU3 in anticipation.

Thanks!

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2b95ae8-b0a3-45b6-bc00-03217d8a7c10)

Fig 1. Modification of the wobble uridine (U34) in mitochondrial and bacterial tRNAs.

Schema of the U34 modification pathways in human and yeast mt-tRNAs and Escherichia coli tRNAs (A) and A. suum mt-tRNAs (B). In A, proteins GTPBP3, MTO1, and TRMU (also named MTU1) from humans, and MSS1, MTO1, and MTU1, from yeast, are orthologous of the bacterial MnmE, MnmG and MnmA proteins, respectively. Taurine (humans) and glycine (E. coli and yeast) are used to introduce the τm and cmnm groups into position 5 of U34. In B, MTCU-1, MTCU-2 and MTTU-1 are the nematode orthologues of GTPBP3, MTO1, and TRMU, respectively, and their roles are inferred from studies of the E. coli and yeast proteins. The fractions of A. suum modified mt-tRNAs, according to the study by Sakurai et al. [[28](https://journals.plos.org/plosgenetics/article?id=10.1371/journal.pgen.1006921#pgen.1006921.ref028)], are indicated below the schema. Note that mt-tRNAGlu, mt-tRNALys and mt-tRNAGln are fully modified at position 5 but lack thiolation at position 2, whereas most (~90%) is modified at both positions (2 and 5), and about 50% of mt-tRNATrp molecules do not contain any modification at the U34.

author: ValWood
body:
Yes, it's the orthologous enzyme, same position, but slightly different substrate residue.

Human is GO:0061708 tRNA-5-taurinomethyluridine 2-sulfurtransferase ( τm⁵U)
Yeast is GO:0103016 tRNA-uridine 2-sulfurtransferase activity (cmnm⁵s²U34 (not τm⁵U)

cmnm⁵s not τm
Taurine (2-aminoethanesulfonic acid) is a sulfonic acid-containing amino acid found abundantly in animals, especially in tissues like heart and muscle.

Taurine is not synthesized or used by most fungi, including budding yeast (e.g., Saccharomyces cerevisiae) or fission yeast (e.g., Schizosaccharomyces pombe).

Yeasts lack the biosynthetic pathway to make taurine, and their metabolism does not rely on sulfonic acid-containing amino compounds like taurine.

Consistent with this, τm⁵s²U (taurinomethyl-2-thiouridine) is not found in yeast mitochondrial tRNAs. Instead, yeast uses alternative modifications, such as mnm⁵s²U or cmnm⁵s²U, depending on the organism and context.

The pombe/S. cerevisiae annotations are fixed above and @Antonialock  is looking into the Rhea/Expasy updates.
I requested a taxon restriction for yeast.

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Hello,
I have attempted to understand the issue here. After rereading the relevant articles several times, I believe we can make some progress. The problem stems from a misinterpretation of the PMID:15509579 paper, which does indeed show reaction with cmnm⁵s²U34 in yeast and  with τm⁵U in human (evidence IMP for the latter). However, the yeast UniProt entry was curated with τm⁵U and used to propagate the information to all eukaryotic members of the MTU1 family.  
I therefore modified the yeast annotation and replaced EC=2.8.1.14 by EC=2.8.1.13.
I annotated the human entry to EC=2.8.1.14 with evidence IMP from the same paper. 
I then propagated the information from the human or yeast annotation to the respective appropriate entries. This resulted in the update of 11 Swiss-Prot entries.
For PAINT, I created a GO annotation for human entries to propagate the right term in the corresponding node. 
For the moment I used EC=2.8.1.13 and associated reaction [Rhea:47032] since I did not find the reaction with cmnm⁵s²U34.
Could someone confirm that this reaction has been requested, if not this has to be done. 
@kaxelsen ?
Once done, we can further update the fungal (and maybe other) entries.
Thanks,
Marc.
